header:
Date: 2027-06-25
Time: 09:30 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Roberts (Redwood AE), Luis Mendez (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Aurora PM), Ravi Patel (Aurora Eng), Tanya Brooks (Aurora Security)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review integration progress: SDK usage for tool/function calls, structured output formatting, and initial perf results. Agreed next steps for benchmarks, security details, and sample data. Customer leaning toward Dedicated for predictable latency but needs cost tradeoffs and security documentation.
topics: SDK integration status: function/tool calling and structured output
Performance results: latency percentiles, throughput, cost estimates
Security and compliance: audit logs, KMS, VPC/private deployment
Next steps: benchmarks, docs, pilot pricing
transcript:
[00:00:01] Jamie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're going to run through the integration status and the results from this week. Luis will cover the perf then we'll go into the SDK bits.
[00:00:18] Maya: Thanks, Jamie. Quick note, we've got someone from security on the call, Tanya, to go over audit/log questions.
[00:00:30] Jamie: Perfect. Luis, you want to kick off with the latency numbers?
[00:00:36] Luis: Yeah, sure. So we ran two passes with Aurora's test trace — first on Redwood hosted API and then on Dedicated with 2 GPUs. Median latency on hosted was around 180-200ms for the short chat flows, p95 was ~420ms. On Dedicated we're seeing median ~120ms and p95 ~260ms with the current batching. Note there's some variance because of sequence length distribution in the trace.
[00:01:05] Ravi: Quick Q — are those numbers with prefix caching enabled?
[00:01:09] Luis: Good call, so the hosted runs had prefix/KV cache partially enabled; the Dedicated runs fully used the KV cache hits we configured. The trace has a fair amount of repeated prompts so cache helps a lot.
[00:01:22] Maya: When you say KV cache, do you mean Redwood's key-value cache or something in our infra?
[00:01:27] Luis: Redwood's KV cache in the runtime — sometimes transcribed as k-v cash on the notes, sorry — it holds token prefixes to avoid recomputing.
[00:01:33] Tanya: From security side, can you confirm what data is stored in the cache and how long it persists?
[00:01:39] Luis: Right now caching keeps non-sensitive prefixes ephemeral; we can configure TTLs or disable it. For PII we recommend client-side redaction or using the Private deployment where you control storage.
[00:01:52] Jamie: To add, we support KMS integration for encryption at rest and an option for on-prem/private if regulation demands.
[00:01:58] Maya: Good. Back to the perf: did you test with function/tool calls in the loop or just straight generation?
[00:02:04] Luis: Both. We instrumented SDK function calls to an external product-metadata service — that adds ~40-60ms overhead per tool call depending on network. The structured output path (we return a JSON schema) has similar generation latency but it's slightly higher if we validate the schema in the SE layer.
[00:02:22] Ravi: Are the SDK examples available? We tried the snippets but hit an error with the tool call glue code.
[00:02:28] Jamie: I sent a small patch to the SDK doc yesterday, we'll re-share. Luis, can you mention the common pitfall?
[00:02:34] Luis: Yeah, in the current Node SDK snippet the function name param needs to be exact and the structured output requires the tools array to be included in the options, otherwise the runtime does not route. Many devs forget the content-type header when calling from serverless envs. Also some transcriptions change Redwood product names — it's 'tool call' pattern in the SDK.
[00:02:53] Maya: That matches what Ravi saw. The error was "missing tool context".
[00:02:57] Ravi: Also we saw occasional tokenization differences where structured output keys were slightly renamed, probably from the model.
[00:03:03] Luis: Right, to mitigate we recommend using the structured output schema enforcement feature — you define a schema and the runtime does a best-effort, plus we provide post-generation validation hooks.
[00:03:13] Tanya: For audit, we need immutable logs with request metadata. Does Redwood have an option for retention and export to our S3?
[00:03:20] Jamie: Yes, audit logs can be exported; retention policies are configurable on Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have export hooks and a compliance add-on. We'll send the SOC2 pack.
[00:03:30] Maya: Excellent. On cost — your estimates for Dedicated vs Hosted earlier looked like Dedicated has higher fixed cost but lower per-token for our traffic patterns?
[00:03:39] Luis: Exactly. With predictable throughput Dedicated usually gives lower per-token after commit. Hosted easier to start and good for bursty small workloads. We put numbers in the spreadsheet but we need to run them with your exact trace for accuracy.
[00:03:51] Ravi: Can you run a sensitivity analysis with 2x traffic and with quantized model variants?
[00:03:56] Luis: Yep, we can. Quantized variants drop RAM/GPU footprint and reduce cost but may impact quality slightly. We'll run both so you can see quality vs cost.
[00:04:05] Maya: Timeline check — we're aiming to decide on Dedicated trial by mid-July. Is that still plausible?
[00:04:11] Jamie: Yes, mid-July decision window is doable. Key blockers: perf numbers with your trace, security sign-off, and pilot pricing.
[00:04:19] Tanya: On security sign-off, we need to confirm KMS binding and HSM support for Private. Also SCIM/SSO integration details.
[00:04:27] Jamie: We'll share integration docs for SAML/SCIM and KMS/HSM specifics.
[00:04:32] Ravi: About SDK function calls — we're trying to chain tool calls: call external inventory service, then generate user message with filled slots. Sometimes the function call returns null fields. Any best practices?
[00:04:44] Luis: Two things: ensure the tool schema is strict so model knows expected fields, and use explicit grounding prompts to avoid hallucination. Also use the 'tools-first' option in SDK so you get deterministic function outputs before generation.
[00:04:58] Maya: Can you show us an example of SDK code that does tool calling and returns validated JSON?
[00:05:03] Luis: I'll paste a gist — but high level: SDK.call({model: 'redwood-llama-v2', tools: [inventoryTool], functions: [{name: 'fill_slots', schema: {...}}], structured_output: {schema: jobSchema} }) — small differences across languages but same pattern.
[00:05:20] Ravi: The node example we used didn't include structured_output param, that's why it failed.
[00:05:24] Jamie: We'll send corrected snippets for node/python and a quick-start sample app.
[00:05:30] Maya: Any quality regressions observed after using quantized model?
[00:05:34] Luis: Slight regression on entity extraction tests — F1 dropped 1.8 points for heavy L2 quant; recommend running your eval sets. That's why we request the sample dataset so we can run the eval harness.
[00:05:47] Tanya: For logs, we need per-token billing detail and traceability back to the request ID.
[00:05:52] Jamie: We provide token-level breakdowns in Console and can map to request IDs; we'll include an example export.
[00:05:59] Maya: On-role mapping — we need RBAC for our internal teams.
[00:06:03] Luis: Console supports RBAC and SSO groups. For Dedicated/Private we can sync with SCIM.
[00:06:09] (small cross-talk)
[00:06:20] Jamie: Alright, for the pilot we'll do these deliverables: 1) Luis runs Dedicated vs Hosted perf tests with Aurora trace; 2) Jamie sends pricing + SDK snippets + security docs; 3) Aurora shares sample data.
[00:06:33] Maya: Sounds good. One more question — can you do a short demo of structured output validation on the next call?
[00:06:38] Luis: Yes, we can do a 20 minute demo focusing on the schema enforcement and tool chaining.
[00:06:44] Ravi: Also please include the error handling patterns for partial tool failures.
[00:06:48] Luis: We'll show retries and fallback to simpler prompts.
[00:06:52] Jamie: Great. Any blockers from Aurora?
[00:06:55] Maya: Just internal legal needs to see data handling docs before we move forward.
[00:06:59] Jamie: We'll attach the data handling and SOC2 docs to the follow-up email.
[00:07:04] Tanya: Please include the encryption-at-rest and KMS binding details.
[00:07:07] Jamie: Will do.
[00:07:10] (silence / typing)
[00:07:20] Maya: Ok, thanks everyone.
[00:07:22] Jamie: Recap: action items and next steps sent in chat. We'll share the SDK patches and schedule the structured output demo for next week.
[00:07:30] Ravi: Thanks all.
[00:07:32] Jamie: Thanks, meeting adjourned.

Note: transcription has minor recognition issues (product names and acronyms), timestamps are approximate and sections abridged for clarity.
